Incremental two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test

Source: R/dfr_iks.R
iks.Rd

A sketch of two samples A (group 0) and B (group 1) that supports the insertion and removal of observations in O(log N) expected time and gives the two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistic D = max |F_A(x) - F_B(x)| in O(1) (dos Reis et al., 2016).

Usage

iks(ratio = 1, seed = NULL)

iks_add(sketch, x, group, tie = 0)

iks_remove(sketch, x, group, tie = 0)

iks_statistic(sketch)

iks_kuiper(sketch)

iks_test(sketch, ca = 1.95)

iks_ca(alpha)

Arguments

ratio

The constant ratio r = |A| / |B| at which the statistic is computed (1, the default, for samples of equal sizes). Each observation of B weighs r.

seed

Seed of the private generator (Park-Miller) of the priorities of the treap and of the tie-breaking values; NULL draws it from R's generator. The priorities do not change the statistic.

sketch

An iks sketch.

x

The observation.

group

0 for sample A (the reference), 1 for sample B.

tie

Tie-breaking value of the observation (0 by default; a random value, as stats::runif(1), makes keys distinct). An observation is removed with the same x and tie it was inserted with.

ca

Coefficient of the critical value ca sqrt((n + m) / (n m)); the default 1.95 is the one of the paper and of the reference code (alpha = 0.001).

alpha

Significance level.

Value

iks() returns an iks sketch; iks_add() and iks_remove() the updated sketch; iks_statistic() the statistic D; iks_kuiper() the Kuiper statistic (max G - min G) / |A|; iks_test() TRUE when the null hypothesis of equal distributions is rejected; iks_ca() the coefficient c(alpha) = sqrt(-log(alpha / 2) / 2).

Details

Observations are sorted by the key (x, tie, group). The treap stores, at every observation, G = F'_A - F'_B (the counts of A minus r times the counts of B up to and including it); an insertion adds 1 or -r to every later observation with a lazily propagated bulk operation, and the subtree maxima and minima give D = max(max G, -min G) / |A|.

As noted by the authors, the statistic is exact only when the observations are distinct: with tied values it can be larger than the one of stats::ks.test(). A random tie value per observation (as IKSSW of the reference code) breaks the ties.

References

dos Reis, D. M., Flach, P., Matwin, S. and Batista, G. (2016). Fast unsupervised online drift detection using incremental Kolmogorov-Smirnov test. In Proceedings of the 22nd ACM SIGKDD International Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining, 1545-1554. doi:10.1145/2939672.2939836

Examples

set.seed(1)
a <- rnorm(200)
b <- rnorm(200, 0.3)
sketch <- iks()
for (i in 1:200) sketch <- iks_add(iks_add(sketch, a[i], 0), b[i], 1)
iks_statistic(sketch)
#> [1] 0.195
unname(ks.test(a, b)$statistic)
#> [1] 0.195
# slide the window of B by one observation
sketch <- iks_add(iks_remove(sketch, b[1], 1), 2, 1)
iks_test(sketch, ca = iks_ca(0.001))
#> [1] TRUE
